catalog_quote: Wisdom 1940, Author's Preface: "Results of studies in the Chorti language will appear in a separate publication; but, since some Chorti terms are mentioned in the text, a description of the phonetic alphabet employed will be useful. ... Diphthongs consist of a, e, and o plus i or u, and of u plus i, with stress on the first element (falling diphthongs), even when final or before final x or h ... The glottal stop, after and between vowels, is very weak; vowel plus glottal stop seems to vary freely with long vowel, with a faint rearticulation after the glottal stop ... Stress is always on the last syllable and is unmarked." ALMG Gramatica Descriptiva 1.2.7: "Entre algunas formas de acentuación que se encuentran en los idiomas mayas están: a) Algunos se acentúan en la sílaba más pesada de cada palabra. b) Otras se acentúa en la última vocal de cada palabra, considerándose como sílaba tónic…

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: Wisdom 1940's 'Stress is always on the last syllable and is unmarked' and the falling-diphthong sentence are verbatim in the held archive.org scanned at Author's Preface pp. ix-x; ALMG 2004 sec. 1.2.7 and Marhenke's preface are verbatim in copies we hold, and a clean native-text ALMG PDF downloaded now shows the same passage (p. 29-30). The weakness is the kind of deciding source, not its content: an ethnographer's phonetic note (1940) plus a community grammar sketch. tone.quote: La prosodie des langues cholanes est encore très peu étudiée. Seul le ch’orti’, avec les travaux de John Fought (1967 et 1972), a fait l’objet d’une analyse systématique de ses accents lexicaux. ... De cette analyse, il ressort que l’accent lexical tombe inconditionnellement sur la dernière syllabe de chaque mot. Les seules exceptions à cette règle concernent les mots empruntés. ... si chaque mot plurisyllabique ch’orti’ porte un accent fixe, ces accents sont hiérarchiquement secondaires par rapport à l’accent qui porte sur le dernier mot d’un groupe de mot ... Cet accent syntagmatique provoque une montée de la fréquence fondamentale toujours plus importante que celles des accents de mot.
tone.locator: vol. I, sec. 1.4 'Quelques elements prosodiques' + 1.4.1 'Ch'orti'', pp. 129-130 of the LOT; laryngealized VV + rising F0 under final accent: sec. 1.3.3.2.1, printed
tone.translation: The prosody of the Cholan languages is still very little studied. Only Ch'orti', with the work of John Fought (1967 and 1972), has had a systematic analysis of its lexical accents. ... From this analysis it emerges that the lexical accent falls unconditionally on the last syllable of each word. The only exceptions to this rule concern borrowed words. ... if every polysyllabic Ch'orti' word bears a fixed accent, these accents are hierarchically secondary to the accent borne by the last word of a word group ... This phrasal accent causes a rise in fundamental frequency that is always greater than those of the word accents.
tone.summary: No lexical tone posited; fixed word-final stress + phrase-final accent (F0 rise); rising F0 on laryngealized VV under stress is phonetic.
